set.explanation: Every assessed pair is consistent under the stated rules.

properties.label: Proposed host galaxy

compat.reason: The reference row for this table (the first active row).
Differently named hosts (MCG +00-10-020 vs PGC013898); they may be aliases or different galaxies.

properties.rule: Two proposed hosts agree when their names match after case and spacing are ignored or one name is among the other's NED cross-identifications; otherwise they are an identity ambiguity. Association probabilities are not computed.

rules.classification: Spectroscopic classes and alert or messenger labels are different definitions and are not compared; two active classes differ when neither label refines the other (for example 'SN Ia' and 'SN Ia-91T' agree); an earlier value from the same provider is a revision.
rules.host: Two proposed hosts agree when their names match after case and spacing are ignored or one name is among the other's NED cross-identifications; otherwise they are an identity ambiguity. Association probabilities are not computed.
rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. The limiting magnitude or flux that a provider reports alongside a detection is that epoch's detection threshold, not a non-detection, and is not compared with the detection; a detection brighter than another provider's non-detection limit at the same epoch is a status conflict. A group is listed only when it is still inconsistent under these rules; at most 10 groups per event, most significant first.
rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).

runs.claimBoundary: A ranking of retained catalogued galaxies under stated priors; the most probable candidate is a suggestion for follow-up, not a host identification, and a host fainter than the catalogues or outside their cones is always possible.
runs.notComputedReason: no catalogued galaxy is retained around the event (NED/SIMBAD/Gaia cones)

rules.missed: a host not in the retained catalogues counts as one candidate at f = missedFractionalOffset
rules.offset: f = separation / directional light radius (SIMBAD shape), else separation x kpc/arcsec(z) / physical scale, else separation / angular scale; term exp(-f); f > maxFractionalOffset gives 0
rules.probable: the top candidate is 'probable' when its posterior >= probablePosterior and >= probableRatio x the next hypothesis
rules.redshift: only when the transient and the candidate both have a redshift: exp(-0.5 (dz / sigma)^2), sigma^2 = sum of the stated errors^2 + floor^2

runs.claimBoundary: Retained earlier detections at the position; they show earlier variability at the position, not that the same source caused both.

parameters.rule: prior activity = at least minDetections detections (S/N >= 5) on at least minNights nights more than gapDays before discovery

runs.claimBoundary: Galactic foreground extinction and a star-like Gaia source at the position; context for reading the photometry, not a classification.

inputs.sfdMap: SFD (1998) via the pinned reference data of Track 3c part 1

rules.point-source: a Gaia DR3 source within pointSourceRadiusArcsec with star probability >= starProbability, or a significant parallax or proper motion

warnings: Pan-STARRS point-source classifications are not retained by CTAS; the point-source flag uses Gaia DR3 only

identity_resolution.policy: Provider and exact source-native alias are the lookup key; unscoped collisions return every candidate and never guess.

inputs.inputRule: ZTF g/r/i difference-PSF detections (ALeRCE, Fink, Lasair; one row per exposure) and ATLAS o/c forced-PSF detections, AB, uncertainty <= 0.5 mag

runs.claimBoundary: A phenomenological fit to public difference and forced photometry; it describes the light-curve shape and is not a classification, a physical model or a distance.
runs.notComputedReason: fewer than two bands with 3 detections

parameters.sharedParameters: timing (and the plateau slope s) shared across bands; one amplitude per band

runs.claimBoundary: A phenomenological fit to public difference and forced photometry; it describes the light-curve shape and is not a classification, a physical model or a distance.
runs.notComputedReason: fewer than two bands with 3 detections

parameters.model: F_b(t) = A_b (1 + s(t-t0)) / (1 + exp(-(t-t0)/tau_rise)) for t < t0+gamma; A_b (1 + s gamma) exp(-(t-t0-gamma)/tau_fall) / (1 + exp(-(t-t0)/tau_rise)) after
parameters.sharedParameters: timing (and the plateau slope s) shared across bands; one amplitude per band

runs.claimBoundary: A phenomenological fit to public difference and forced photometry; it describes the light-curve shape and is not a classification, a physical model or a distance.

parameters.colourScreen: the per-epoch colour and blackbody temperature are the collector's multiband screen under analysis_screens
parameters.modelChoice: the multiband fit with the lower AICc

runs.claimBoundary: A phenomenological fit to public difference and forced photometry; it describes the light-curve shape and is not a classification, a physical model or a distance.
runs.notComputedReason: no peak magnitude (the light-curve features were not computed)

parameters.kCorrection: +2.5 log10(1+z) bandwidth term only; no spectral k-correction

runs.claimBoundary: A phenomenological fit to public difference and forced photometry; it describes the light-curve shape and is not a classification, a physical model or a distance.
runs.notComputedReason: no band has a detection in the last 2 days and 3 detections 10-70 days earlier

runs.claimBoundary: A phenomenological fit to public difference and forced photometry; it describes the light-curve shape and is not a classification, a physical model or a distance.
runs.notComputedReason: no band has 20 detections over 30 days

parameters.detrending: magnitudes minus the chosen multiband fit when one exists (a transient's own rise and fall is not a period)
parameters.periodicCandidateRule: FAP < 1e-3, best period shorter than a third of the span, and the frequency not within 0.02 day^-1 of the 1, 2 or 3 day^-1 sampling aliases

runs.claimBoundary: Screens that point at candidates for a closer look (kilonova-like timescales, nuclear position); they are not classifications.

rules.fast-transient: shared-shape half-maximum rise < 3 d or 15-day decline > 0.3 mag/day
rules.nuclear-transient: a retained NED host offset, or the offset of the probable host of host_association (posterior rule stated there), < 0.5 arcsec
